Getting started with TOP

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

TOP fits two-stage polytomous logistic regression models for case-control studies in which cases are characterized by multiple disease or tumor markers. The recommended interface for new analyses is top_fit().

Data layout

The outcome matrix has case-control status in its first column (0 for controls and 1 for cases) and tumor characteristics in the remaining columns. Tumor characteristics must be NA for controls. If case tumor characteristics can be missing, use a distinct numeric code and pass it as missing_value.

library(TOP)
data("data", package = "TOP")

y <- data[, 1:5]
snp <- data[, 6, drop = FALSE]
pc1 <- data[, 7, drop = FALSE]

head(y)
#>      case.control ER PR HER2 grade
#> [1,]            0 NA NA   NA    NA
#> [2,]            0 NA NA   NA    NA
#> [3,]            1  1  0    1     1
#> [4,]            1  1  1  888   888
#> [5,]            1  1  1    0     0
#> [6,]            0 NA NA   NA    NA
table(y[, 1])
#> 
#>    0    1 
#> 4888 5112

The simulated package data use 888 for missing case tumor characteristics.

Fit an additive model

Here the SNP and principal component both use an additive second-stage structure. top_fit() validates dimensions, coding, missingness, and finite covariate values before calling the numerical model.

fit <- top_fit(
  y = y,
  additive = cbind(snp, pc1),
  missing_value = 888
)

fit
#> TOP two-stage polytomous model
#> Observations: 10000  Tumor markers: 4 
#> Log-likelihood: -16726.5  AIC: 33514.9

Results have stable names. The second-stage table contains baseline case-control effects and marker-specific case-case effects.

Standard R methods are also available.

head(coef(fit, stage = "second"))
#> [1] -3.581787 -3.799975 -4.021544 -4.638728 -3.177350 -4.688342
dim(vcov(fit, stage = "second"))
#> [1] 31 31
summary(fit)
#> TOP model summary
#> Call: top_fit(y = y, additive = cbind(snp, pc1), missing_value = 888)
#> Log-likelihood: -16726.5  AIC: 33514.9 
#> 
#> Global tests:
#>   Covariate Global test for association Global test for heterogeneity
#> 1       SNP                     0.05430                         0.126
#> 2       PC1                     0.00563                         0.251

Choose a second-stage structure

Covariates can be assigned to different structures:

  • baseline: a common association across subtypes;
  • additive: baseline plus tumor-marker main effects;
  • pairwise: additive effects plus pairwise marker interactions;
  • saturated: a separate effect for every retained subtype.

For example, a common SNP effect can be adjusted for an additive PC effect.

fit_mixed <- top_fit(
  y = y,
  baseline = snp,
  additive = pc1,
  missing_value = 888
)

Subtype counts and convergence

TOP historically omits subtypes with counts at or below the cutoff. The default subtype_cutoff = 10 preserves that behavior. Lower cutoffs can make information matrices unstable, particularly in small datasets. Numerical failures raise R errors instead of terminating the R session.

Set options(TOP.verbose = TRUE) temporarily when EM progress messages are useful.

Existing scripts

TwoStageModel() remains available for backward compatibility. New code should prefer top_fit() and named components such as fit$second.stage.test rather than positional indexing.
